summary: Flushes file buffers for an open file identified by index a1. Validates a1 against the open file count uNumber (008D4A20) and against the slot's active flag bit 0 in the per-slot descriptor array, enters the per-file critical section, resolves the OS handle via sub_595A1F, calls FlushFileBuffers, and reports failures through the TLS slot getters (error code 9 for the generic path, GetLastError for the extended path). Returns 0 on success and -1 on any guarded failure. Called by MemoryBlockValidationCheck (0058A02C).

local_names.v1: per-slot byte offset within the descriptor block (36 * (a1 & 0x1F))
local_names.v2: OS file HANDLE obtained from the file index
local_names.LastError: captured GetLastError after a failed flush

operations.description: Guard a1 < uNumber (008D4A20); an out-of-range index falls through to the error path.
Guard the active-flag bit 0 at descriptor-block offset 4 (descriptor base selected by a1 >> 5, slot offset 36 * (a1 & 0x1F)); the slot must be open/active.
CriticalSectionEnterWithLazyInit(a1) enters the per-file critical section with lazy initialization.
Re-check the active-flag bit 0 inside the critical section; if it is no longer set, fall through to the TLS error-9 path.
sub_595A1F(a1) translates the file index into an OS file handle.
FlushFileBuffers(handle) flushes the file buffers to disk.
If FlushFileBuffers succeeds LastError stays 0; otherwise GetLastError captures the failure code.
On a failed flush, write the captured GetLastError value into the TLS slot returned by TLSOffsetGetter_afd8 (extended error info).
On the generic failure path, write error code 9 into the TLS slot returned by TLSOffsetGetter and set the result to -1.
FileCriticalSectionLeave(a1) releases the per-file critical section on the success and failure paths.
Return LastError (0 on success, -1 on the guarded failure paths) to the caller MemoryBlockValidationCheck (0058A02C).

unresolved: The descriptor array base is named dword_8D4920 in the raw source but no corresponding global entry exists in the packet's allowed evidence, so the array base address is not asserted here.
The exact layout of the per-slot descriptor block (36-byte stride, active bit at offset 4) is read from raw offsets and has no named-struct evidence.
The purpose of the TLS error codes (9 generic, GetLastError extended) beyond being set on failure is caller-consumed and not visible in this packet.
